title: variable-pad-trimmer-and-sequence-cohort-allocator
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed persistent padding overhead on workloads with high variance in sequence length (chat + multimodal tokenizers). Existing bucketing strategies reduce padding but leave room for improvement where short-lived short sequences cluster with long sequences in shared slots, causing excess GPU work and KV cache churn. This PR introduces two coordinated heuristics: (1) a Variable Pad Trimmer that opportunistically trims trailing padding at slot boundaries by adjusting KV offsets and kernel work sizes, and (2) a Sequence Cohort Allocator that groups inflight requests into transient cohorts based on a lightweight sequence-length sketch and estimated token-density, prioritizing cohorts for coalesced kernel launches.

Summary of changes: added a new coordinator in the serving runtime (runtime/slot_cohort_allocator.cc/py bindings) that maintains per-slot cohort candidates and drives short-window cohort formation; implemented pad-trimmer code paths in the kernel dispatcher to emit smaller work ranges when trailing pad-only columns are detected; extended the scheduling policy to expose a cohort_hint that can be consumed by the GPU scheduler and packing layer; KV cache metadata now carries a trimmed-offset to allow coherent reuse of cache ranges without copying large tensors. The changes are conservative by default (feature-flagged) and fall back to existing bucketing when heuristics are disabled or not beneficial.

Benchmarks & results: end-to-end benchmarks on prod-like traces (conversation mix, token-density variance 0.18–0.47) show a median token-cost reduction of 9% and p95 latency improvement of 6% for the Canary cluster; synthetic extreme-variance workloads saw up to 14% throughput uplift. Microbenchmarks indicate the pad-trimmer adds ~0.3ms scheduler overhead per batch in worst-case but reduces per-token GPU FLOPs meaningfully for padded slots. Regression tests added to perf-canary and benchmark-lab reproducer scripts.

Compatibility & safety: The code is guarded behind runtime feature flags: cohort_allocator.enabled and pad_trimmer.enabled. KV cache trimming updates maintain backward-compatible metadata layout; we added a compatibility shim in KV cache loaders for older persisted traces. No API changes to the public Redwood API. We included a stress test simulating rapid sequence-length churn to validate correctness and KV coherence.

Why this is different from existing bucketers: Rather than statically bucketing by seqlen or using fixed padding policies, the cohort allocator is a transient, fast-path grouping mechanism that considers short temporal locality (requests arriving within the same slot window) and token-density. The pad-trimmer complements the allocator by reducing wasted compute when cohorts include a mix of short and long sequences that were historically padded to the longest in-slot request.

review_comments: Marco Chen: Nice work. Concern: how do we reason about KV cache fragmentation over long-lived sessions? Can we add bucket-level compaction if fragmentation crosses threshold?

Aisha Patel (author): Fragmentation tracked in serving.pad_trimmer.fragmentation_ratio; added a compaction callback in the compat shim that schedules eviction for low-benefit ranges. Will follow up with an automated compaction PR if we see threshold crossings in canary.
Lena Garcia: Can we get numbers on p50/p95 for short-chat workloads? Also please add a flag to disable pad trimming per-queue for experiments.
Aisha Patel (author): p50/p95 added to description; added per-queue disable in config. Updated tests to cover queue-specific disable.
Tomás Ruiz: tests look good. Please confirm no behavioral change for private deployment (VPC) path.
Aisha Patel (author): Verified locally against private-installer dev image; no API or on-disk layout changes for private deployments beyond the shim. Noted in docs.
merge_result: Merged by Marco Chen (squash merge). Changelog: added section 'cohort allocator & pad trimmer' under runtime performance improvements. Canary rollout started Feb 18.
release_notes: Introducing an optional runtime optimization: Variable Pad Trimmer and Sequence Cohort Allocator. Reduces padding overhead in mixed-length workloads; expected token-cost savings 5–14% depending on variance. Feature flags: cohort_allocator.enabled, pad_trimmer.enabled. Monitor serving.pad_trimmer.* metrics during rollout.
additional_context: Related linear tickets: ENG-4021 (cohort allocator proposal), ENG-4199 (pad trimming design). This PR intentionally keeps behavior behind flags to enable gradual rollout and A/B. Follow-up work: automatic compaction, adaptive cohort sizing, and kernel-level fused trim-and-dispatch path.
